title: NOAA APT Decode Pass Success Rate
dataSources: Aircraft messages (`adsb:message`), APRS packets (`aprs:packet`), AIS vessel messages (`ais:message`), rtl_433 decodes (`rtl433:sensor`), RF occupancy summaries (`sdr:spectrum`), satellite observations (`satnogs:observation`), and repeater use (`repeater:activity`).
app: Radio and SDR telemetry from WSPR, APRS, ADS-B, AIS, rtl_433, SatNOGS, and local receiver health feeds streamed to Splunk HEC via APIs, MQTT, and log shippers.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=satnogs:observation mode="APT"
| stats sum(eval(if(result="success",1,0))) as successful_passes count as passes by satellite
| eval success_pct=round(100*successful_passes/passes,1)
| sort success_pct
description: Calculates weather-satellite pass decode success rates so antenna position and scheduler changes are easy to evaluate.
value: Pass success is a clean end-to-end metric for an SDR receiving setup because it blends timing, RF performance, and local conditions.
implementation: Record each attempted APT pass with mode, result, and satellite name from SatNOGS or your own scheduler.
visualization: Bar chart of successful-pass percentage by satellite.
grandmaExplanation: It maps how often your weather-satellite setup turns a pass into a usable image instead of a miss.
